sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which traditional game involves tapping a teammate on the back and shouting 'Kho'?
What is the primary focus of 'Pranayama' in Yoga?
In the game of Kabaddi, what must the raider constantly do while in the opponent's court?
Which of these yoga poses is designed to look like a tree and improves your balance?
What is a major physical benefit of playing traditional games like Tag or Hide and Seek?
options: B) It builds speed, agility, and stamina
C) It helps you learn to read faster
questions.answer: B) It builds speed, agility, and stamina

questions.question_text: Which posture is best used for completely relaxing the body at the end of a yoga session?
Which traditional Indian game uses a small oval-shaped wooden piece and a larger wooden striking stick?
What should you always do before starting a vigorous traditional game or a yoga stretching session?
options: D) Sit still for an hour

questions.question_text: How should you breathe while holding a stretching posture in Yoga?
options: B) Breathe very fast and shallow
D) Only breathe through your mouth

questions.question_text: In a game of Tug of War, what physical quality is most needed by the team?
Why is warming up important before playing Kabaddi or performing Yoga? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Warming up stretches the muscles, increases blood flow, and prepares the body. This helps prevent painful injuries during stretching or fast movements.

questions.question_text: Briefly describe how to play the traditional game of 'Gilli Danda'. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Players use a long wooden stick to strike a smaller oval-shaped wooden piece. The primary goal is to hit the small piece as far as possible.

questions.question_text: Name two benefits of practicing the Tree Pose (Vrikshasana) every day. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Practicing the Tree Pose daily greatly improves physical balance, strengthens the leg muscles, and helps increase your mental focus and concentration.

questions.question_text: How does teamwork help in a traditional game like Tug of War? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: In Tug of War, teamwork ensures everyone pulls the rope at the exact same time. This combined strength easily overpowers the opposing team.

questions.question_text: What is the correct way to sit while doing simple breathing exercises (Pranayama)? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Sit comfortably on the floor with your legs crossed. Keep your back completely straight, rest your hands gently on your knees, and close your eyes.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are leading a game of 'Kho-Kho'. Describe the setup and the basic action of passing the turn. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The sitting team kneels in a straight line, facing opposite directions alternately. When the active runner wants to pass the turn, they tap a sitting teammate gently on the back and loudly shout 'Kho', signaling them to get up and chase.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are demonstrating the 'Shavasana' (Corpse Pose) to your class. Describe how they should lie down and relax. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Lie flat on your back with your legs slightly apart and arms resting loosely by your sides, palms facing upwards. Close your eyes, breathe slowly, and let every muscle in your body feel heavy and completely relaxed against the floor.

questions.question_text: Explain the physical actions and mental focus required by a raider in the game of Kabaddi to score a point and return safely. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The raider must take a deep breath and continuously chant 'Kabaddi' without stopping. They must use quick footwork to dodge defenders and stretch their arms to tap an opponent. Mentally, they need sharp focus to watch the defenders' movements closely, while staying constantly aware of the midline to escape safely back home.

questions.question_text: Describe the complete sequence of actions to perform a simple standing forward bend (Padahastasana) safely, focusing on breathing and stretching. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Stand tall with your feet together. Inhale deeply while raising both arms straight above your head. Slowly exhale as you bend forward from your hips, keeping your legs straight but not stiffly locked. Reach your hands towards your toes or the flat floor, relaxing your neck completely, and hold this soothing stretch calmly.
